🌍 Justice must never be biased or shaped by political considerations: Iran Judiciary Chief

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s Judiciary Chief, Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje’i, has called for a fair international legal order, stressing that justice must not be selective, subordinate to political considerations, or determined by countries’ levels of power and influence.

Speaking at the opening ceremony of the BRICS meeting of heads of judicial systems in New Delhi on Saturday, Mohseni-Eje’i said adherence to law is a fundamental pillar of justice, order and progress.
​
The senior official argued that respect for international law can help prevent unilateralism, coercion and the imposition of powerful states’ excessive demands on others.
​
He said BRICS, as an influential economic and political block, has repeatedly emphasized mutual respect, national sovereignty, territorial integrity, peaceful settlement of disputes and adherence to the United Nations Charter.
​
Mohseni-Eje’i called on BRICS members to support an international order in which no power considers itself above the law.
​
He also criticized widespread violations of human rights and humanitarian law, unilateral sanctions and attacks on independent nations, urging judicial and legal entities to respond to violations involving civilians, forced displacement, damage to infrastructure and impunity for perpetrators of international crimes.
​
Referring to recent attacks against Iran, he said the United States and the Israeli regime are committing war crimes and criticized international organizations for failing to respond adequately.
​
The Judiciary Chief urged BRICS members to condemn violations of Iran’s sovereignty and territorial integrity under international law and take measures against aggressors.
​
Mohseni-Eje’i also called for the prosecution, under the principle of universal jurisdiction, of those responsible for war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the conflicts against Iran.

Debt is becoming too expensive, and now the government will be looking for ways to make it cheaper.

And the more interventions like this we see, the stronger the fear that the dollar will lose value. That’s why some of the money is moving into gold and Bitcoin.

Which, as a result, saw inflows of $7 billion in just 5 days.

At the same time, no one is giving up on AI either. Nvidia keeps climbing, and money is still flowing into tech funds.

The market is now simultaneously buying AI as a bet that technology will make the world richer, while also buying gold and Bitcoin as insurance in case the bill for this party turns out to be too big and the system can’t handle it.

Thailand. From September 15, visa-free stay is 30 days again, not 60

The special 60-day regime that was granted to citizens of about 93 countries since July 2024 is being cancelled. The new rules will start from September 15, 2026. Until this date, 60 days are still given at the border.

What's changing:
• Most countries, including Russia, USA, EU, UK, Australia - visa-free stay of 30 days.
• Seychelles and Mauritius - 15 days.
• Visa on Arrival is being limited; countries like Azerbaijan, Belarus, Serbia remain on the list.
• Those already in the country on a 60-day stamp can complete their stay. There is no retroactive effect.
• DTV, LTR, Privilege, work, pension - remain unchanged.

Why: in May, the government decided to close the gap for visa-runners, nominal tourists, and those living in the country for months. The usual package vacation (~9 days) is almost unaffected.
For Russians, the visa-free stay is not being canceled - they are simply returning to the old 30-day limit under a bilateral agreement.
